text:
mike: Heads-up — canary nodes in us-central are seeing multi-GPU inference workers hang after nccl 4.1.1 + CUDA 12.2 bump. Hangs happen only on mixed NVLink+PCIe pods. :frowning:

lucy: Repro on local a100 cluster?

mike: Yes, repro on 4/8 card configs. Steps: start gpt-serve with batch 8, tokens ~512, then one worker's allreduce hangs and the rest spin. No OOM.

jess: Any dmesg or kernel oops?

mike: dmesg shows repeated peer-to-peer timeouts and mmap faults. snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] nv_peer_mem: p2p mapping failed: -71
[ 1234.568000] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: nvlink: link error - reset
```

omar: Could be driver/kernel ABI mismatch. Which kernel on canary?

mike: 6.5.9 on canary, prod mostly 6.1.27. Repro doesn't occur on 6.1.

karen: We rolled nccl 4.1.1 and matching nvidia driver 535.113.02? Did we also change module params or firmware?

mike: Yep driver bump. Regression seems to appear only when iommu is enabled + THP on. Workaround tried: echo 0 > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled reduced hangs but not eliminated.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-15T09:12:00 completed with nccl-4.1.1

lucy: We should collect per-node /var/log/nvidia-installer and nccl trace. Also capture /proc/iomem and lspci -vv.

jess: Proposal: pin canary back to nccl 4.1.0 and driver 535.100 for now. Create rollback runbook?

mike: Agree. Impact: ongoing canary instability forces us to throttle capacity; estimated 6% capacity loss if we drain affected nodes. Cost impact small but risk for customer SLAs.

omar: I'll open a ticket with vendor. Assigning to @nvidia-eng with logs and mmap backtraces. Also test with kernel 6.1 and 6.4 to narrow.

karen: Can we add a temporary scheduler rule to avoid placing mixed nvlink/pci pods on the same node? Maybe taint nodes with 'p2p-unstable=true'.

mike: created ticket INFRA-1284. For now toggled taint on canary pool and scaled down inference jobs. Monitoring for 30m.

lucy: If anyone sees hang again, run:
```
sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -o /tmp/perf.data sleep 60
sudo nccl-tests/all_reduce -b 8 -e 64M -f 2
```

jess: Thanks. Keep posting short updates. :thumbsup:
